questions.title: What is the difference between HTML and XHTML?

rows.text: XHTML (eXtensible HTML) is a markup language that follows the rules of XML to define the structure of a web page.
Doctype is not necessary to write at the top.
Doctype is very necessary to write at the top of the file.
HTML has lenient syntax - Closing tag is not mandatory for some elements.
XHTML follows stricter syntax rules. - All tags must be properly nested and closed.
All tags and attributes are not necessarily to be in lower or upper case. - HTML is not case-sensitive
Every tag and attribute should be in lower case. - XHTML is case-sensitive
HTML is widely supported by all browsers and web platforms
XHTML has limited support by browsers.

questions.title: How can you apply JS in your HTML? / Where to place JS link reference?

content.text: Scripts can be placed inside the body, the head section of an HTML page, inside both head and body, or can be added externally.
If JS functions are not manipulating HTML elements then you can place it inside the head section.

If JS functions are manipulating HTML elements then place the JS reference link at the end of the body section - because head will load before the body. So till the control reaches the reference link, all the elements will be loaded.

JavaScript can also be used as external files. JavaScript files have file extension .js . To use an external script put the name of the script file in the src attribute of a script tag. External scripts cannot contain script tags.

questions.title: What do you mean by manifest file in HTML5?

content.text: manifest file is a text file that tells the browser to cache certain files or webpages so that they can be used even in offline mode.
HTML5 cache webpages by specifying manifest attribute in <html> tag.
All the web pages that contain manifest attributes or are specified in the manifest file will be cached whenever a user visits that page.
MANIFEST keyword and contains three sections:
: This section lists all the resources including webpages, CSS stylesheets, JavaScript files, and images that will be cached immediately after their first download.
: This section lists all the resources that will never be cached - can’t be used in offline mode and always require a connection to the server.
: This section lists the fallback resources that will be used in case a page is not accessible.

questions.title: Explain Web Worker in HTML.

content.text: in HTML is a feature of the Web API that allows you to run JavaScript in the background, separate from the main thread of a web application.
This helps improve the performance and responsiveness of your application by offloading resource-intensive tasks (like calculations, data processing, or API calls) to a worker thread.
: Runs tasks in the background, independent of the main UI thread.
: The main thread remains free for UI updates and user interactions.
: Communicates with the main thread using the
: Workers cannot directly access the DOM or certain browser APIs, ensuring thread safety.
e.g. : One worker handling a specific task for a single web page.
Can be shared across multiple scripts and browser tabs or windows.
e.g. : A worker managing a shared state between multiple tabs.
Primarily used for intercepting network requests and caching resources for offline use.
